description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely in the context of feedback incorporation as suggested by the paper title. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” ranges from 0.81 to 0.99 and is presented on a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and is also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three distinct lines: the “Final Accuracy” (blue line with solid circles) starts at approximately 1.0 and remains mostly above 0.85, showing minor fluctuations; the “Δ Accuracy” (orange line with diamond markers) begins at approximately 0.45, dips to a low of about 0.05 near 0.89, and then gradually declines to approximately 0.02 by 0.99; the “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers) starts at approximately 0.55, rises to a peak of about 0.90 near 0.90, and then gradually declines to approximately 0.90 near 0.99. All lines are plotted with error bars indicating variability.
